preview: The Tour opens with a team time trial for the first time since 1971. Mostly flat along the Mediterranean coast before two categorized climbs in the final 4km — the Côte de Montjuïc and a short, steep ramp to the Olympic Stadium — where each rider's individual time is taken.
source_notes: Distance confirmed at 19.6km (cyclingstage.com, franceletour.com); some sources round to 19.7km. Start time 17:05 CEST, last team off ~19:16 confirmed by idlprocycling.com. First TTT tour-opener since 1971.

preview: 85km of flat roads along the Costa Dorada before the terrain kicks up. Two finishing laps around Montjuïc in Barcelona, including the steep Côte du Château de Montjuïc, set up a punchy finish likely to see early GC skirmishes.
source_notes: Distance 168.5km confirmed across cyclingstage.com, cyclingflash.com, cyclingnews. Some early aggregator sources (domestiquecycling, franceletour) listed 178-182km — likely rounding/draft-route errors; 168.5km matches the user brief and multiple dedicated route-detail sources, treated as authoritative.

preview: The Tour crosses into France on stage 3, its first true mountain test. Demanding Pyrenean terrain straddling the Spain-France border culminates in an uphill finish at Les Angles, likely to produce the first real GC gaps.
source_notes: Distance 195.9km confirmed (cyclingstage.com). Elevation ~3850-4000m depending on source; used 3850m as middle estimate. Summit finish at Les Angles ~6.5% per user brief.

preview: A rolling route through Cathar country in the Pyrenean foothills. A string of minor climbs favors a breakaway, with a final categorized climb roughly 35km from the finish that could tempt puncheurs to attack late.
source_notes: Distance 181.9km matches user brief and domestiquecycling (182km rounded). Elevation gain estimated (~2800m) — not explicitly published; treat as estimate.

preview: The first true sprint opportunity of the race. After several demanding early stages, sprinters' teams are expected to control the day and set up a mass bunch finish in Pau.
source_notes: Distance 158.3km per cyclingstage.com (158km per domestiquecycling). Elevation gain estimated — no significant categorized climbs reported.

preview: A full Pyrenean assault packing three major passes into the final 80km — the Col d'Aspin, the Col du Tourmalet, and a summit finish at Gavarnie-Gèdre. One of the defining GC days of the opening week.
source_notes: Distance 186.2km per cyclingstage.com. Elevation >4100m per domestiquecycling; matches user brief summit-finish list.

preview: A second sprint opportunity through the forests of the Landes toward Bordeaux. Little terrain to trouble a well-drilled peloton; a mass bunch sprint is the likely outcome.
source_notes: Distance 175.1km per cyclingstage.com. Flat, sprint stage.

preview: A second consecutive sprint stage through the Dordogne wine country. Fast run-in expected to leave a breakaway little chance, with points classification contenders battling over two intermediate sprints.
source_notes: Distance 180.4km per cyclingstage.com (182km per domestiquecycling, rounding difference).

preview: The opening week closes with a lumpy, unrelenting route through the Corrèze department — no flat kilometres and roughly 3,400m of climbing. A stage that could suit a strong breakaway or provoke fireworks among GC riders before the rest day.

climbs.name: Côte de la Croix de Pey

source_notes: Distance 185.5km per cyclingstage.com. Elevation ~3400m per domestiquecycling ('no flat km' description).

preview: A Bastille Day mountain stage through the Massif Central with seven categorized climbs, including the iconic Puy Mary and Pas de Peyrol, before a summit finish at the Le Lioran ski station. Vingegaard beat Pogačar on this finish in 2024.

climbs.name: Le Lioran (finish climb, via Col de Font de Cère)

source_notes: Distance 166.6-167km depending on source. Elevation ~3,791-3,900m confirmed by multiple sources. Note: cyclingstage.com classifies this as 'Hills' but it has a summit finish and is one of the 8 mountain stages / 5 summit finishes per official race framing and most previews (domestiquecycling, velo.outsideonline) — classified here as mountain.

preview: A third sprint opportunity coming out of the rest day, with a small late climb unlikely to trouble the sprinters' teams. Bunch finish expected in Nevers.
source_notes: Distance 161.3km per cyclingstage.com. Elevation ~1800m per domestiquecycling.

preview: Starting from the former Formula 1 circuit at Magny-Cours, a largely flat run toward Chalon-sur-Saône. A late minor climb is unlikely to prevent a bunch sprint finish.
source_notes: Distance 179.1km per cyclingstage.com (181km per domestiquecycling).

preview: The longest stage of the 2026 Tour at 205.8km, entering the Vosges via the Ballon d'Alsace, the first significant mountain terrain since the Massif Central. The early summit likely favors a breakaway over the GC group.
source_notes: Distance 205.8km confirmed as the Tour's only stage over 200km. Elevation gain estimated (~2600m) — not explicitly published in sources reviewed.

preview: Seven ascents in the Vosges, four of them in the final 60km, including the Grand Ballon and a summit finish at Le Markstein Fellering. Multiple steep ramps exceeding 9-10% should keep the GC battle wide open.
source_notes: Distance 155.3km per cyclingstage.com. Elevation ~3800m per domestiquecycling. Note: this stage climbs the Ballon d'Alsace on both stage 13 and stage 14 approaches per sources — flagged as possible source inconsistency but retained as reported.

preview: The route escalates ahead of the final rest day, finishing on a brutal new summit at Plateau de Solaison with sustained gradients around 9-11%. Expect the GC picture to be seriously reshuffled right from the base of the final climb.
source_notes: Distance 183.9km per cyclingstage.com. Elevation ~4700m estimated (franceletour.com cites 11.3km/9.1% for final climb vs domestiquecycling's 11.6km/8.9% — minor gradient discrepancy between sources, both indicate a very steep new summit finish).

preview: The Tour's sole individual time trial and the shortest in the modern era, coming right out of the second rest day. An early categorized climb followed by a flat lake-shore run to Thonon-les-Bains makes this more than a pure rouleur's course.
source_notes: Distance 26.1km per cyclingstage.com (26km per user brief). Matches known ITT stage from Évian to Thonon.

preview: Only nominally flat — rolling Alpine foothill terrain with a shallow climb before the finish makes this the sprinters' last realistic chance before the mountain finale begins. Expect the sprinters' teams to fight to keep the race together, and a reduced bunch sprint if they manage it.
source_notes: Distance 174.7km per cyclingstage.com (175km per domestiquecycling). Classified as hilly/rolling given ~2200m elevation despite being billed as a 'sprinters' stage'; some sources call it flat.

preview: A historic venue echoing Luis Ocaña's legendary 1971 ride. A gentler approach than that famous stage, but still likely selective, with a summit finish at Orcières-Merlette after climbs including Engins and Monteynard.
source_notes: Distance 185.2km per cyclingstage.com. Elevation ~3950m per franceletour.com. Some sources list intermediate climbs as Col de Manse / Col du Festre rather than Engins/Monteynard — naming discrepancy between sources, both sets retained is not possible so domestiquecycling's climb list used.

preview: A short but ferocious stage — early climbs including the Col du Noyer set up an explosive day well before the legendary 21-hairpin finale up Alpe d'Huez, the first of back-to-back summit finishes there. At barely 128 km there is nowhere to hide, and the overall contenders will be marking each other from kilometre zero.
source_notes: Distance 127.9km per cyclingstage.com. Alpe d'Huez climb figures cross-checked: Wikipedia cites 13.8km/7.9%, domestiquecycling cites 13.9km/8% — used Wikipedia's figure as primary. First of the historic back-to-back Alpe d'Huez summit finishes.

preview: The queen stage and hardest day of the race by a wide margin, with roughly 5,600m of climbing across the Col de la Croix de Fer, Col du Télégraphe, Col du Galibier (the Tour's highest point) and Col de Sarenne, before a second consecutive summit finish atop Alpe d'Huez. Whoever wears yellow will have to earn it twice on the same climb in two days — this is where the 2026 Tour is most likely won or lost.

climbs.name: Col de la Croix de Fer

source_notes: Distance 170.9km per cyclingstage.com (171km per domestiquecycling). Elevation 5,600-5,601m confirmed across multiple sources as the queen stage. Second consecutive Alpe d'Huez summit finish, first time in Tour history back-to-back finishes on the same climb.

preview: The traditional processional-then-competitive finale, modified again to include three ascents of the Butte Montmartre before a flat 15km run to the Champs-Élysées. Race director Christian Prudhomme has said the strongest sprinters will still have a chance despite the climbs.
source_notes: Distance 130km per domestiquecycling/franceletour, 133km per cyclingstage.com — minor discrepancy, likely reflects late course finalization; used cyclingstage.com's more recent figure. Montmartre climbs repeat the format introduced in 2024 Olympics/2025 Tour finale. Start time later than other stages (afternoon finish for TV/ceremony purposes) per franceletour.com schedule.
